title: Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic back one AI training opt-out
content:
Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic will honour one shared AI training opt-out in robots.txt. It lets a website keep its content out of generative AI training with a single rule. Today, a site that wants to say no has to write separate rules for each company’s crawler.
The shared signal comes from an IETF draft by Kevin Kelley of Anthropic, published on Friday. The same day, Google, OpenAI and Microsoft announced they would support it. Kelley announced the draft on the IETF’s AI preferences mailing list.
It works through robots.txt, the file sites already use to tell crawlers what they may fetch. A site adds a group for a new “policy token”, __usage_ai-training. It then lists the paths it does not want used for training. The draft’s example blocks a whole site except its press kit.
“Publishers should not have to choose between being discoverable in Bing and deciding how generative models use their work,” Krishna Madhavan, principal product manager for Microsoft Bing, wrote.
Who starts when
Anthropic has already started work on it, Kelley wrote. He said it would complement Anthropic’s existing crawler controls rather than replace them.
“It’ll take us some time to add support across our services and work through the inevitable complications and edge cases that I’m sure we’ll discover,” Kelley wrote.
OpenAI said it aims to implement the signal “in the coming months”. Its existing crawler controls, such as GPTBot, will still apply, it said.
Google said it aims to support the signal in 2027, and its crawler documentation says early 2027. Google-Extended is Google’s own AI training control. If a site opts out with the token and does not mention Google-Extended, Google will treat it as a block on Google-Extended. Sites that allow Google-Extended can appear in Gemini app answers and get clicks, Google Search Advocate John Mueller wrote.
Microsoft will honour the new preferences from 1 February 2027. They will replace the NoArchive and NoCache tags it has used since 2023. Microsoft is also adding a separate page-level setting for grounding, when an AI answer draws on a live web page. One option allows Microsoft’s own products, such as Copilot. It blocks the grounding services Microsoft sells to other companies.
What the signal does not do
The draft says the token states a preference about how sites want their content used. It is not an order about crawling. A site with no such group has expressed no preference, and existing rules for all crawlers do not count. Private agreements between a site and an AI company can override it.
The draft is an individual submission. The IETF’s datatracker says the IETF has not endorsed it and it has no formal standing in the standards process.
Microsoft said the new preferences “do not establish licensing or payment arrangements”. Blocking AI grounding “will significantly reduce your content’s visibility in AI-generated experiences”, it added. It does not change a page’s place in Bing search results.
Meta communications head Andy Stone voiced support for a common signal on X, The Verge reported. He did not say whether Meta would honour it.
The European angle
Google said the proposal is consistent with the EU’s Code of Practice for general-purpose AI under the AI Act. The code recognises robots.txt as a main way for publishers to state machine-readable preferences.
Among the people the draft thanks for shaping the discussion are staff from the Financial Times, the BBC, Bertelsmann and the European Publishers Council.
Publishers have also pushed for payment. In July, Cloudflare told AI crawlers to pay or get blocked. Its chief executive has warned that bots could reach 1,000 times human web traffic. In Australia, the ABC and SBS want AI companies to pay for news.

report.summary: 四大AI公司统一robots.txt退出信号，网站一条规则即可拒绝AI训练
report.background: 长期以来，不希望内容被用于AI训练的网站必须在robots.txt里为每家公司的爬虫分别写屏蔽规则，如GPTBot、Google-Extended，维护成本高且容易遗漏。Anthropic的Kevin Kelley于上周五在IETF提出个人草案，新增统一策略标记__usage_ai-training，让站点一次性表达训练偏好。同日Google、OpenAI、微软宣布支持，Anthropic已着手开发。此举发生在出版方持续施压的背景下：Cloudflare在7月要求AI爬虫付费否则封禁，澳大利亚ABC与SBS也要求AI公司为新闻内容付费。
key_points: 新规则沿用网站已有的robots.txt：增加一个__usage_ai-training分组并列出不想被训练使用的路径，无需再为每家爬虫单独写规则。
各家落地时间差别很大：Anthropic已开工，OpenAI称“未来数月”，微软2027年2月1日，谷歌要到2027年初，短期内旧爬虫规则仍是主力。
该标记只是表达偏好而非强制命令：它不限制抓取，未声明的站点等于没有表态，站点与AI公司之间的私下协议可以推翻它。
微软同时新增页面级grounding开关：可允许Copilot等自家产品引用，同时屏蔽卖给第三方的接地服务，但屏蔽会显著降低内容在AI回答中的曝光。
草案属个人提交，IETF未背书、在标准流程中无正式地位；谷歌称其与欧盟AI法案的通用AI行为准则方向一致。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，内容授权从逐家谈判走向机器可读的统一协议，为后续标准化和潜在付费机制铺路，但2027年前的空窗期意味着实际保护有限。对开发者，抓取合规判断更简单，但需要处理“有偏好无偏好”的模糊语义，并注意微软新增的grounding开关。对普通用户，短期内几乎无感，长期可能导致部分优质内容不再出现在AI回答中，或推动AI公司转向授权内容和自有数据。
report.tools: 想跟进的读者可研究robots.txt规范与IETF草案原文（AI preferences邮件列表）、Google-Extended与GPTBot的官方文档、Cloudflare的AI爬虫管控与pay-per-crawl方案，以及WordPress等CMS的robots.txt管理插件，便于快速为站点配置统一退出信号。
